summary: Ephemeral proxy path drift leads to partial streaming fragment and out-of-order resume for long SSE sessions
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed that long-running SSE streaming sessions from our hosted API sometimes reconnect to a different edge proxy instance (ephemeral proxy path drift) and when that happens the resumed stream contains a truncated fragment and the final sentence is duplicated or arrives out-of-order. Impact: partial outputs or duplicated concluding sentences cause downstream ingestion/parsing errors in customer pipelines (JSONL and NLP post-processing).

Observed behavior:
- After a network hiccup and client reconnect, the resumed SSE emits a fragment that appears to be missing the last 8-12 tokens of the previous tail and then replays a short prefix before continuing.
- The duplicated prefix sometimes appears in the middle of the final paragraph, breaking JSONL lines.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should stitch previous tail and resumed payload cleanly: no token loss, no duplicated tokens, and ordering preserved.

Notes: Customer uses Dedicated capacity in us-east, long-running prompts (~30s generation), client-side keepalive 15s, and an intermediary corporate proxy that performs occasional short-lived connection handoffs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use LinguaTech sandbox account on dedicated pool in us-east to start SSE generation with a long prompt that produces ~600-800 tokens over 30-45s.
2) Simulate a short NAT or path change (client IP rebind) or force a transparent proxy rebind on the path between browser and edge (customer provided repro steps: toggle VPN for 2s).
3) Immediately reconnect the client using same session id/resume token and resume the SSE stream protocol.
4) Observe resumed stream: check final chunks for missing tokens and duplicated short prefixes; capture full raw SSE events and compare sequence numbers/offset headers.

2026-03-10T14:12:39Z [serving-runtime-9] resume request session=abc123 offset=594 resume-token=rt-XX status=200

investigation_notes: Initial triage: Support verified payload corruption happens only when a client reconnects and the resume path crosses a different edge proxy instance (edge-proxy-18 -> edge-proxy-23).

Hypothesis A: Edge proxy handshake or partial buffer flush leaves last byte as incomplete UTF-8 codepoint which causes serving-runtime to emit a replacement char (�) and then subsequent chunking logic misaligns resume offset.
Hypothesis B: Corporate intermediary rewrites or strips/changes Content-Length/transfer-encoding causing downstream chunk coalescing to occur differently on new path.

Evidence: logs show 'altered Content-Length header' from edge-proxy-23 proxied request and serving-runtime emits 'last-char=�' on resumed chunk. Customer's network team confirmed an inline proxy which performs HTTP header normalization on reconnections.
Repro test: We replayed session with a local proxy that rewrites header and reproduced truncation + duplicated prefix within 3 runs. When header rewrite was disabled, resume stitched cleanly.

Metrics: spike in SSE resume errors correlated with edge-proxy handoffs; dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streams/sse-resume?orgId=1 shows resume-fail-rate increase aligned to 2026-03-10 14:10-14:20 UTC.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:02 - Ben Park (Support): Thanks for the clear repro, LinguaTech team. We've started an internal repro and see mismatch on resume when edge path changes. Can you confirm whether the corporate proxy does any header re-writing or content inspection?
2026-03-10 16:10 - LinguaTech (Customer): Confirmed — our gateway normalizes content-length for connections that re-establish under a different path. We can toggle off for testing.

2026-03-10 17:25 - Clara Mendes (SRE): Repro'd locally with header rewrite. Root cause appears to be that when the previous connection ended mid-multibyte character, edge proxy flush plus header normalization causes serving-runtime to treat the resumed first chunk as a fresh chunk rather than an extension — offset bookkeeping gets misaligned by 1-2 bytes.

2026-03-11 09:30 - Ben Park (Support): Short-term workaround provided to customer: set client-side keepalive to 5s and enable 'resume-strict' flag in SDK to buffer last 2kb and perform client-side checks for incomplete UTF-8 sequences before sending resume. Customer confirmed reduced incidence during A/B test.

2026-03-12 11:40 - Clara Mendes (SRE): Deployed proxy hardening change to edge-proxy that preserves trailing byte boundaries on chunked responses and avoids Content-Length rewriting for SSE/resume requests; PR linked.
resolution: Root cause: Header normalization by intermediate proxies combined with edge-proxy handoff produced chunk boundary changes and left incomplete UTF-8 codepoints unhandled during resume which misaligned resume offsets and produced duplicated/truncated fragments.

Mitigation applied: 1) Quick workaround documented for customer (reduce keepalive, enable resume-strict client-side buffer). 2) Server-side fix: edge-proxy will now mark resume-capable connections and preserve trailing partial bytes across handoffs (edge-proxy PR https://github.com/redwood/edge-proxy/pull/87). 3) Serving-runtime change to validate and reassemble UTF-8 boundaries on resume before emitting tokens (inference PR https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4213).
Rollout: fix deployed to us-east edge fleet on 2026-03-12 10:50 UTC behind feature flag; monitored for 24h — no further repros from LinguaTech after deployment.

Follow-up actions: create guidance page on recommended corporate-proxy settings for SSE/resume and add an SDK helper that validates/trims incomplete UTF-8 suffix prior to resume. Confluence doc created and linked.
notes: This ticket highlights interplay between customer network appliances and our resume semantics; will add a desktop tool to help customers detect dangerous proxy behaviors pre-deployment.
CS will follow up with LinguaTech to schedule a short audit of their proxy behavior and offer configuration guidance.
